1.s: “Return to me, and I will return to you.” A night vision of horsemen among myrtle trees: the world is at rest, but God is jealous for Jerusalem and will comfort Zion.
1.d: The first message is dated October 520 BC, the second year of Darius [[tbd:026:Zechariah, Book of]]. It urges the people to repent and not repeat their ancestors’ mistakes [[tbd:026:Zechariah, Book of]].

2.s: A man measures Jerusalem, but it will be a city without walls, for God will be a wall of fire around it. Many nations will join themselves to God.
2.d: Whoever touches Israel touches “the apple of his eye”: harming God’s people brings his judgement [[tosn:Zechariah 2:8]].

3.s: Joshua the high priest stands in filthy clothes, accused by Satan; God gives him clean garments and promises “my servant, the Branch”.
3.d: Joshua’s filthy clothes stand for the guilt that led to exile; removing them shows God taking sin away [[tosn:Zechariah 3:2–3]] [[tosn:Zechariah 3:4]]. The coming king is called the Branch [[tosn:Zechariah 9:9]].

4.s: A gold lampstand fed by two olive trees: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit.”
4.d: God by his Spirit would help Zerubbabel and Joshua rebuild the temple [[tosn:Zechariah 4:1–14]]. The lampstand recalls the tabernacle menorah [[tosn:Zechariah 4:2–3]]; Revelation 11:4 also speaks of two olive trees [[bible:Revelation 11:4]].

5.s: A flying scroll of curses, and a woman in a basket representing wickedness carried off to Babylon.
5.d: The flying scroll reminded the returned exiles that the law’s blessings and curses still applied [[tosn:Zechariah 5:1–4]].

6.s: Four chariots go out to the whole earth. Joshua is crowned as a sign of the Branch who will build the temple and be priest on his throne.
6.d: Joshua’s symbolic crowning as king and priest likely points to the coming Messiah [[tosn:Zechariah 6:9–15]]. Hebrews presents Jesus as both [[bible:Hebrews 7:1-3]].

7.s: Asked about fasting, God says what he wanted was justice, mercy and care for widows, orphans, foreigners and the poor.
7.d: Zechariah challenges their motives: if they did not want to please God, fasting did not matter [[tosn:Zechariah 7:4–7]] [[tosn:Zechariah 7:1–8.23]].

8.s: God promises to return to Zion: old people will sit in the streets and children play. Ten men from the nations will take hold of a Jew’s robe, saying, “We have heard that God is with you.”
8.d: The fasts will become feasts when God restores Israel and shows his glory to the nations [[tosn:Zechariah 8:19]].

9.s: “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion!… Behold, your King comes to you! He is righteous, and having salvation; lowly, and riding on a donkey.” He will speak peace to the nations.
9.d: Chapters 9–14 carry no dates and do not name Zechariah; most scholars think they come from later in his ministry [[tosn:Zechariah 9:1–14.21]] [[tbd:026:Zechariah, Book of]]. The humble king is the coming Son of David [[tosn:Zechariah 9:9]], and Matthew connects him with Jesus’ entry into Jerusalem [[bible:Matthew 21:4-5]].

10.s: God, not idols, gives rain. He will strengthen his people and gather them like a shepherd.
10.d: A rebuke of false shepherds, leaders who use their people [[tosn:Zechariah 10:1–3]].

11.s: Zechariah acts as a shepherd and is paid thirty pieces of silver, which he throws to the potter in the temple.
11.d: Thirty pieces of silver was the price of a slave; the Gospel writers see this fulfilled in Judas’s betrayal [[tosn:Zechariah 11:12]].

12.s: God will defend Jerusalem, and pour out a spirit of grace; “they will look to me whom they have pierced; and they shall mourn for him.”
12.d: The New Testament reads the one who was pierced as Jesus [[tosn:Zechariah 12:10]] [[bible:John 19:37]].

13.s: A fountain will be opened to cleanse from sin. “Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.”
13.d: A fountain for cleansing, fulfilled in the new covenant [[tosn:Zechariah 13:1]]. Jesus quotes 13:7 on the night of his arrest [[bible:Mark 14:27]].

14.s: The day of Yahweh: God stands on the Mount of Olives, living waters flow from Jerusalem, and “Yahweh will be King over all the earth.” Even the pots will be holy.
14.d: Living waters from Jerusalem stand for God’s presence among his people (Ezekiel 47; Revelation 22) [[tosn:Zechariah 14:8]].
